units.en: and finally in our boolean logic section we have this BitmaskExample.c in the code we have a which is set to some hex value, b which is set to some hex value and then an if statement where it takes and it does a bitwise and on a and b and then based on whether or not that's zero or non-zero it's going to return 0x70dd1e or 0x707 so we can tell just by looking at the values that are operated on that it's definitely going to return non-zero but the interesting thing about this example is

even though this is a bitwise and here we don't see a bitwise and in the assembly instead what we see is a test instruction so what is the test instruction so the test instruction according to the manual computes a bit wise and of the first operand and second operand and sets the flags accordingly so test is similar to cmp in that cmp was behind the scenes actually a subtract instruction that throws away the result after setting the flags test is an and instruction that throws away the result

after setting the flags.
